Subject: Renewal window — proposal to transition to hybrid 18mo with mid-term uplift

Priya / Karthik,

Hope you both are well. Nebula's renewal is up for 11/15 and we've been modeling a couple of choices with finance. We're leaning toward a structure that: (a) co-terms to our fiscal Q1 start, (b) gives an 18-month initial term with an option to extend to 36 months at a mid-term uplift, and (c) stages capacity increases in two ramp buckets (months 1–6: 40% of forecast; months 7–18: 75% of forecast).

I've attached a draft onramp workbook (Nebula_Onramp_Draft.xlsx) with our forecast and preferred billing cadence. Key asks:
- Can Redwood provide a blended price for an 18mo base with a 2nd-period uplift schedule?
- Is a co-term to our FY Q1 (starting 2027-01-01) feasible without proration mechanics that create billing spikes?
- Do you have a compact amendment template we can use so procurement can move quickly?

We prefer auto-renew toggled off; Nebula wants a clear uplift trigger (usage bands and a simple true-up). Lastly, SOC2 evidence and a short statement on data retention are required for our security review — can you point me to the current package?

Thanks — happy to hop on a 30-min call if that's easier.

Alex
Director of Platform Ops
Nebula Analytics

Attachments: Nebula_Onramp_Draft.xlsx (spreadsheet, 1 sheet)

From: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Renewal window — proposal to transition to hybrid 18mo with mid-term uplift

Alex — thanks for the workbook and clear asks. Quick response at a high level, and I attached a short proposal that maps the buckets to pricing and billing cadence (Redwood_Renewal_Proposal_v1.pdf).

High-level proposal notes:
- Hybrid structure: 18-month firm term with an optional 18-month extension that can be executed at month 12 via an agreed uplift schedule. The uplift is structured as a percentage on the base per-token rate and applies only to incremental capacity beyond the month-12 baseline.
- Co-terming: we can co-term to your FY Q1 start with a pro-rated alignment invoice to avoid a large one-time charge — we propose smoothing the pro-rate over the next 3 invoices instead of a single bucket.
- Ramp buckets: we can lock guaranteed capacity for months 1–6 at 40% of your 12-month ARR forecast and then step to 75% for months 7–18. Excess usage is billed monthly as overage at the agreed overage rate.
- Auto-renew: default off. We'll include an auto-renew opt-in checkbox for the renewal amendment and Mirror the uplift trigger logic in the SOW.

I'll call out two internal follow-ups: pricing desk needs to confirm the uplift percentages (range we propose is +8% to +14% depending on volume bands), and legal will draft a short amendment template. Karthik — can you confirm if we can offer a frontloaded credit option (first 3 months) to help with Nebula's cashflow? Marissa — can you review the proposed amendment language for procurement speed?

I've also uploaded the SOC2 summary and retention checklist to our shared folder (link below) — see Redwood_SOC2_Summary.pdf. Happy to jump on a call Friday morning PT if that works for you.

Thanks,

Subject: Internal: pricing option for Nebula hybrid term (for Priya)

Priya / Marissa — quick internal note on pricing options for Nebula. Two paths we can take: 1) 18mo base + optional 18mo extension at a mid-term uplift (Priya's proposal) or 2) 36mo committed term with frontloaded credits spread across months 1–6 (helps the customer's cashflow and reduces churn risk). Pros/cons: 36mo gives us better revenue visibility but reduces flexibility for the customer; 18→36mo keeps the door open and matches Nebula's ask.

If we go with option 2 (36mo), I'm willing to structure a 3-month credit equal to ~20% of month 1–3 expected usage and bake a quarterly true-up. That would require a security/finance sign-off and a short amendment with explicit mid-term true-up language. Marissa — can you confirm how fast legal can provide a compact amendment (our procurement rapid template)?

I'll be out for a short window on Monday afternoon but can join a call Tuesday if needed.

—Karthik
VP, Sales Operations
